summary.title: Intro to Angular and the Evolution of the Web
summary.one_liner: Learn why frontend frameworks like Angular emerged to reduce backend dependence, and what single page applications (SPAs) are and how Angular builds them.
takeaways: Frontend frameworks such as Angular can move interactive work from the backend to the browser.
Angular is an open source, Google-made frontend framework for SPAs and succeeds AngularJS, but is not backward compatible with it.
Angular uses TypeScript to add type safety, which compiles to plain JavaScript that runs in modern browsers.
Angular organizes views into components and uses dependency injection and services, with lifecycle hooks for setup and teardown.
A SPA can have many views and URLs but loads its resources once instead of reloading pages from the server.
summary.summary: This introductory article traces how the web's frontend has changed, arguing that developers often pushed interactivity to the backend because JavaScript lacked modules, OOP and type safety. It then introduces Angular (described as major version 5 at the time of writing) as an open source framework for single page applications, covering its use of TypeScript, RxJS, components, dependency injection, services and lifecycle hooks. The author also clears up the misconception that SPAs have only one URL and view. It is a conceptual overview with no code samples, and it says the next article in the series covers getting started with Angular.
